title: ChatGPT for Sales: Pricing and Integrations (2026)
summary: ChatGPT for sales works with automation scripts and platforms. Its usefulness hinges on integration with your existing tools.
body_markdown:
## ChatGPT for Sales claims that can be checked


None of the page's claims is yet confirmed here to the level you would wire a workflow against. It makes a handful of checkable ones about a sales plugin, partner plugins, listed apps, a customer result and seat pricing.


That's why each one gets read against the page before anything's built.


### ChatGPT for Sales plugins and listed apps


The page describes a sales plugin and a set of partner plugins that connect it to other tools, plus a list of apps it works with.


A catalogue count tells you nothing about the trigger that starts a run, the action that writes back, or which fields map across. Until the page names those, treat the list as a menu of logos.


It also cites a result from a customer, NeoBid. That's the vendor's own framing of one deployment, so it says little about your pipeline, and nothing about what the customer automated to get it.


If a plugin sits behind a particular plan, or the connected apps need admin approval, a pilot can stall at the first permissions screen. Availability is the line to pin down before anything else.


The page as read on 2026-11-18 doesn't give me a plan-by-plan breakdown I can confirm, so I won't invent one.


The page gives seat pricing: $20 per user per month billed annually or $25 billed monthly for a standard seat. Seat pricing also leaves open whether connected apps, automated runs or API calls carry separate charges.


A per-seat quote covers the person typing, not the workflow running overnight. Get the metering terms in writing before costing a rollout.
